title: Convergence rate of the (1+1)-evolution strategy on locally strongly convex functions with Lipschitz continuous gradient: the martingale strong-law convergence rate proposition (Proposition 2)
author: Daiki Morinaga, Kazuto Fukuchi, Jun Sakuma, Youhei Akimoto
work: Convergence rate of the (1+1)-evolution strategy on locally strongly convex functions with lipschitz continuous gradient
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Proposition 2 (source0.tex lines 455--475, source label prop:convergence_rate), which packages the convergence-rate analysis of the (1+1)-evolution strategy into three checkable conditions on a Markov chain: given a filtration and a Markov chain adapted to it, if C1 (a uniform upper bound on the expected one-step decrement) and C3 (square-summability of the variances divided by t^2) hold, then the almost-sure limsup of (X_t - X_0)/t is at most -B^upper, and if C2 and C3 hold then the almost-sure liminf is at least -B^lower; it is delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 2410--2425 (the appendix subsection "Proof of Proposition 2", 16 lines). The proposition is the article's declared central tool: the article introduces it with the sentence "Our main mathematical tool to derive bounds for the upper and lower convergence rate of the (1+1)-ES is the strong law of large numbers on martingales [7]. It reduces the analysis of the limit behavior to the analysis of the expected sequence change in one step. The following proposition is the central tool for our analysis", and both of the article's main theorems (its upper convergence rate bound and its lower convergence rate bound) are proved by verifying C1--C3 and applying it. The author proof is complete and closed inside the retained span: it forms the martingale difference sequence Z_{t+1} = X_{t+1} - E[X_{t+1} | F_t], decomposes (X_t - X_0)/t into the martingale average plus the average of the conditional expectations, uses the variance decomposition Var[X_t] = Var[Z_t] + Var[E[X_t | F_{t-1}]] >= Var[Z_t] to see that C3 implies the square-summability of E[Z_t^2]/t^2, applies Chow's strong law of large numbers for martingales to get the almost-sure vanishing of the martingale average, and then takes limsup with C1 and liminf with C2 to obtain statements (I) and (II). The argument is short but it is a genuine research-paper step: the choice of the variance condition C3 exactly so that Chow's theorem applies, and the passage from the one-step expected change to the almost-sure asymptotic rate, are the content of the paper's method rather than a routine verification. H2: an original research proposition with a complete author proof, depending on one quoted external theorem (the cited martingale strong law).
